getRepoLink.title: How to get a GitHub repository link.
getRepoLink.intro: RepoContext works with any link in the form
getRepoLink.introSuffix: . Here is exactly how to copy one in five steps.

steps.title: Open the repository on GitHub
steps.desc: Go to github.com and open the repository you want to analyze. It can be your own repo or any public one — for example the link shown on the homepage: https://github.com/psf/requests.
steps.tip: Public repos work with no setup. For private repos, connect your GitHub account first.

steps.title: Copy the URL from the address bar
steps.desc: Once you are on the repository's main page, look at your browser's address bar. The full URL there is your repository link. It always follows the pattern https://github.com/owner/repository — for instance https://github.com/vercel/next.js.
steps.tip: Just copy the whole address — no extra parameters or tokens are needed.

steps.title: Make sure you are at the repo root
steps.desc: The link should end with owner/repository only. If you clicked into a file or folder, the URL will contain extra segments such as /blob/, /tree/, or /issues/. Click the repository name at the top of the page to get back to the root before copying.
steps.tip: Wrong example: https://github.com/psf/requests/blob/main/requests/api.py — go up to the root first.

steps.title: Optional: point to a specific branch
steps.desc: By default RepoContext analyzes the default branch. If you want a specific branch analyzed, add /tree/branch-name to the URL — for example https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/develop.
steps.tip: Leave this out unless you specifically need a non-default branch.

steps.title: Paste it into RepoContext
steps.desc: Copy the link with Ctrl+C (Windows) or Cmd+C (Mac), return to the RepoContext homepage, paste it into the input field, and click Analyze. Within a few seconds you'll get AI-ready context for your repository.
steps.tip: That's it — no configuration file or credit card required for public repositories.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.q1: Is my code uploaded to your servers?
faq.a1: RepoContext only reads what it needs from the GitHub API. The full source tree is never written to disk on our side, and you can delete the cached metadata at any time from the dashboard.
faq.a2: Yes — Pro and Team plans support private repos via OAuth. Your code never leaves your control; we only read metadata, not file contents, by default.
faq.a3: Every analysis ships with a quality score. Files with low confidence are flagged in the evidence panel so you know exactly where to double-check.

sections.heading: 1. Acceptance of Terms

The Service is provided “as is” and “as available”. We do not promise uninterrupted or error-free access.

bullets: Keep your password confidential and do not share your account with others.
API keys are displayed once at creation and stored only as a SHA-256 hash. If you lose a key, revoke it and create a new one.

privacy.metaDescription: What RepoContext collects, why, how long it is kept, and the rights you have over your data.
privacy.title: Privacy Policy

sections.heading: 1. Introduction
body: RepoContext (“we”, “our”) turns GitHub repositories into AI-readable context. This policy explains what personal data we collect, why we collect it, how long we keep it and what you can ask us to do with it.

sections.heading: 2. Information You Give Us
bullets: Account data: your email address and a hashed password, managed by Supabase.
Support messages: the message you type into the support widget and, if you provide one, your email address so we can reply.
Waitlist signups: the email address you submit to hear about new features.
Payment data: we never receive or store your card number — Creem handles the transaction and has its own privacy policy.

sections.heading: 3. Information We Collect Automatically
bullets: Analysis data: repository URLs you analyse, the resulting quality score and generated files, stored with your account when you are signed in.
API usage: per-minute request counts used to enforce rate limits, and the last time each key was used.
Log data: IP address, browser and device information, and the pages you visit.
Error reports: crashes and exceptions are sent to Sentry so we can diagnose faults.

sections.heading: 4. Cookies and Local Storage
body: We use a small number of strictly necessary cookies and no advertising or cross-site tracking cookies.
bullets: Session cookie — keeps you signed in.
Language preference — remembers the language you picked.
Trial counter — tracks how many free analyses you have used this month.
Cookie consent — remembers your choice in the consent banner.
Local storage — your most recent analyses are cached in your own browser so results survive a refresh. This data never leaves your device unless you explicitly create a share link.

sections.heading: 5. GitHub Repository Data
body: We read repository metadata and configuration files through the GitHub API. We do not clone or store your full source tree.
For private repositories we only read what your OAuth grant allows, and only after you connect your account.

sections.heading: 6. Shared Analysis Links
body: When you create a share link, a snapshot of that analysis — repository name, quality score and generated context files — becomes publicly readable at an unguessable URL. Anyone with the link can view it.
Do not create a share link for sensitive content. To have one removed, email jpkowton@gmail.com with the URL and we will delete it.

sections.heading: 7. Third-Party Processors
body: We share data with these providers only to run the Service:
bullets: GitHub — reads repository metadata and files.
OpenAI — generates the context files. Repository metadata and file excerpts are sent for processing.
Creem — processes payments and subscriptions.
Supabase — hosts the database and authentication.
Resend — sends transactional email (welcome, receipts, support).
Sentry — collects error and performance reports.
Vercel — hosts and serves the application.

sections.heading: 8. Why We Process Your Data
bullets: To provide the Service you asked for, including running analyses and enforcing quotas.
To keep the Service reliable and secure, and to investigate abuse.
To send service messages you cannot opt out of while you hold an account, such as receipts and security notices.
To comply with legal and tax obligations.

sections.heading: 9. How Long We Keep Data
bullets: Account and analysis history: kept while your account is open, and deleted within 30 days of you deleting the account.
Support messages and waitlist entries: kept until you ask us to remove them.
Shared analyses: retained until removed on request.
API rate-limit counters: discarded after roughly two hours.
Server logs: rotated on a short cycle.

sections.heading: 10. Your Rights
body: Depending on where you live you may have the right to access, correct, delete, export or restrict the processing of your personal data, and to object to processing based on our legitimate interests. You also have the right to complain to your local data protection authority.
bullets: Delete your account and its data directly from the dashboard.
Ask us for a copy of your data, or ask us to correct or erase it, by emailing jpkowton@gmail.com.
We answer requests within 30 days.

sections.heading: 11. Security
body: We use HTTPS everywhere, hash API keys with SHA-256 so the plaintext is never stored, and keep privileged credentials on the server only. No method of transmission over the internet is completely secure, so please protect your own credentials too.

sections.heading: 12. International Transfers
body: Our providers operate globally, so your data may be processed outside your country. We rely on standard contractual clauses and equivalent safeguards where required.

sections.heading: 13. Children's Privacy
body: The Service is not directed at children under 16 and we do not knowingly collect their data. If you believe a child has given us data, email jpkowton@gmail.com and we will delete it.

sections.heading: 14. Changes to This Policy
body: We may update this policy. Material changes are announced on this page and, for signed-in users, by email at least 14 days before they take effect.

sections.heading: 15. Contact
body: Questions about this policy or about your data? Email jpkowton@gmail.com.

bullets: Include the email address on the account and the approximate date of the charge.

aup.metaDescription: The rules that govern what you may analyse, how you may use the API, and what will get your account suspended.
aup.title: Acceptable Use Policy

sections.heading: 1. Scope
body: This Acceptable Use Policy (“AUP”) applies alongside our Terms of Service. If the two conflict on a topic this AUP covers, this AUP controls for that topic.

sections.heading: 2. Prohibited Inputs
body: You may not submit or analyse content that:
bullets: Is illegal where you live or where the content is hosted.
Infringes someone else's intellectual property, privacy or publicity rights — for example code copied from a private repository you have no permission to access.
Is malware, ransomware, exploit code, or anything designed to compromise a computer system.
Facilitates phishing, social engineering or credential theft.
Contains personal data you are not authorised to process under GDPR, CCPA, PIPL or any other applicable privacy law.

sections.heading: 3. Prohibited Uses
body: You may not use RepoContext to:
bullets: Reverse-engineer the Service or try to extract the underlying model weights, prompts or source code.
Probe, scan or load-test our infrastructure.
Bypass rate limits, quotas or payment, including by creating extra accounts, clearing cookies, rotating API keys, or sharing one account between many people.
Resell, sublicense or white-label the Service or its output without written permission.
Use the output to train, fine-tune or improve a competing AI model or product.
Publish an API key anywhere it can be read by others, including committing it to a repository.

sections.heading: 4. Prohibited Outputs
body: You may not:
bullets: Ship generated AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, Cursor Rules or Copilot instructions as part of a paid product without checking their accuracy and security first.
Present generated content as human-authored work in a way that misleads others.
Feed generated content into automated systems that make decisions about people — hiring, credit, housing — without human review.

sections.heading: 5. API and Share Links
body: Public share links are readable by anyone who has the URL. Do not publish a share link that exposes credentials, secrets or content you are not licensed to distribute. We may remove any share link that breaches this AUP.

sections.heading: 6. Rate Limits and Fair Use
body: Anonymous visitors get a monthly quota of free analyses and API keys get a per-minute limit. These exist to keep the Service responsive for everyone. We may throttle, suspend or terminate accounts that exceed reasonable use or that we reasonably believe breach this AUP.

sections.heading: 7. Reporting Abuse
body: If content analysed by RepoContext violates this AUP, or another user is abusing the Service, email jpkowton@gmail.com with a link and a short description. We review reports within five business days.

sections.heading: 8. Consequences
body: Depending on severity we may issue a warning, temporarily suspend the account, terminate it without refund, remove a share link, or refer the matter to law enforcement where required.

sections.heading: 9. Changes to This Policy
body: We may update this AUP. Material changes are announced on this page and by email for signed-in users.

sections.heading: 10. Contact
body: Questions about this policy? Email jpkowton@gmail.com.

howto.title: Turn your codebase into AI-ready context.
howto.subtitle: RepoContext analyses your GitHub repositories and generates accurate, structured documentation for AI coding agents. No setup, no installation.

problems.title: AI hallucinations
problems.desc: LLMs guess your project structure. RepoContext gives them the real structure, dependencies and conventions.

problems.title: Manual documentation
problems.desc: Writing AGENTS.md or Cursor Rules by hand takes hours. RepoContext generates them in seconds.

problems.title: Inconsistent formats
problems.desc: Different AI tools need different formats. Export to AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, Cursor Rules or Copilot Instructions.

steps.title: Copy your GitHub repository URL
steps.desc: Open the public GitHub repository you want to analyse. Copy the URL from your browser address bar — it looks like github.com/owner/repository. Private repositories are supported on paid plans once you connect your GitHub account.

steps.title: Paste it into RepoContext
steps.desc: Return to the RepoContext homepage, paste the URL into the input field and click Analyze. The engine fetches the repository metadata and starts scanning.
steps.tip: No credit card and no configuration file needed for public repositories.

steps.title: Wait for AI analysis
steps.desc: RepoContext detects frameworks, package managers, build tools, CI/CD pipelines, test setups and directory conventions. Every insight is linked to the actual files used as evidence.
steps.tip: Analysis usually takes a few seconds, depending on repository size.

steps.title: Review the quality score
steps.desc: Each report includes a quality score showing how reliable the generated context is. A higher score means the AI had more evidence and fewer uncertain guesses.
steps.tip: Open the evidence list to see which files influenced each insight.

steps.title: Export and integrate
steps.desc: Choose your preferred format and download the file. Drop it into Cursor, Claude Code, GitHub Copilot or any AI coding agent that reads project context.
steps.tip: Supported formats: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, Cursor Rules, Copilot Instructions.
